summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data show generally good CGM coverage (98.7%) with acceptable overall time in range (86.0%) but time below range above typical target (5.1%) and several distinct hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia clusters. No carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the period, so all glucose rises are handled reactively through SMB/UAM rather than meal-announced bolusing, and carb ratio segments cannot be validated. A mid-period Profile Switch event on 2026-08-13 is logged in telemetry, but the user has explicitly declared the current aaps_profile as historically applicable for the full period, so this is treated as one continuous profile rather than segmented. Several notable excursions (2026-08-14 rebound hypo/hyper, 2026-08-19 pump occlusion and error) have plausible non-profile explanations and are excluded from pattern-level conclusions. Dynamic ISF (not Autosens, which is disabled) is actively varying effective sensitivity widely across the period, which plausibly explains inconsistent correction outcomes seen for similarly sized boluses. Given the absence of carb data and the presence of multiple confounders, no profile parameter change is currently well-supported; the most valuable next step is establishing basic meal logging before adjusting basal, CR, ISF, DIA, or automation strength settings.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent (98.7%, 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest 65 minutes, no duplicates or invalid entries), supporting reliable hourly and daily aggregation. Treatment and device-status telemetry is only partially sampled (40 of 2315 treatments; 24 of 6214 device statuses), sufficient for illustrating patterns but not for exhaustive dose reconstruction. Zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere in the period. A Profile Switch event is logged on 2026-08-13, but profile_context explicitly declares historical_applicability as yes for the current aaps_profile; this user declaration is treated as authoritative and overrides any inference from the telemetry linkage event, correcting an earlier working assumption that early-period days might reflect a different unrecorded configuration.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate time below range is 5.1%, above a typical 4% caution threshold, with CV of 32.6% near the upper acceptable boundary. Severe hypoglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21 (as low as 41-42 mg/dL). Severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18 (up to 293 mg/dL). The 2026-08-14 sequence shows a hypoglycemia cluster followed shortly by an aggressive automated correction and rebound hyperglycemia, suggesting overcorrection dynamics rather than a static basal or ISF defect. The 2026-08-19 hyperglycemia coincides with a logged pump Occlusion and Pump Error announcement, a plausible device-related confound. Repeated 135 mg/dL Temporary Targets occur on multiple days when smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, raising an unresolved hypothesis that SMB may be suppressed during these windows.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight hours (00:00-02:00 local, 0.6 U/h basal, 90 mg/dL target) show elevated time below range (11.4%-18.5%) despite near-target averages; this is at least partly attributable to IOB carryover from earlier correction boluses rather than clearly excess basal, and the two explanations are not yet separable. Afternoon hours (12:00-17:00 local, 100 mg/dL target) show the worst glucose control of the day (up to 32.1% time above range at hour 16, coinciding with the 0.5 U/h step-down), plausibly explained by unlogged meals, basal timing, or dynamic ISF behavior, none of which can be isolated without carb data. Evening hours (18:00-19:00 local) again show elevated time below range as basal increases from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h, more likely reflecting residual IOB from afternoon corrections than the small basal step itself. The 10-hour DIA plausibly extends IOB tails contributing to delayed hypoglycemia 120-360 minutes after several corrections.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile uses a single flat ISF value (56 mg/dL/U) by design, but dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with a 70% adjustment factor, so the effective sensitivity used by the loop varies widely across the period (roughly 27.8 to 178.7 mg/dL/U equivalent), which plausibly explains inconsistent outcomes for similarly sized correction boluses. Carb ratio segments cannot be validated at all because zero carbohydrate entries exist in the entire 14-day period; this inference remains blocked, not merely uncertain. DIA (10 hours) plausibly contributes to prolonged IOB tails and delayed hypoglycemia noted in basal_targets, but this is entangled with SMB frequency and dynamic ISF behavior and cannot be attributed to DIA alone.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and active in loop reasoning; because carbohydrate entries are always zero, UAM is functioning as the sole mechanism for detecting unannounced meal-like rises, so both settings appear necessary rather than incidental. SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_temp_target_enabled true) support continuous operation consistent with observed frequent SMBs; smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled are currently moot since COB is always zero. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false while repeated 135 mg/dL temporary targets occur during high-glucose windows, raising an unresolved hypothesis about SMB suppression that cannot be confirmed from the available sampled loop statuses. SMB delivery limits (3-minute interval, 15 and 20 minute basal-minute caps) do not appear to be constraining delivery based on observed dose sizes. Apparent post-hypo rebound hyperglycemia on 2026-08-14 may reflect unlogged rescue carbohydrates rather than an automation overcorrection, and this cannot be distinguished with current data.

analysis_steps.findings: Max basal (12 U/h) and max IOB (25 U) limits are far above observed maxima (peak enacted rate 4 U/h, peak IOB 5.935 U), so these limits are not constraining current dosing and cannot explain the observed excursions. Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is enabled at a 70% adjustment factor, an internally consistent pairing since running both together is generally avoided. sensitivity_ratio values of 1 in most samples are correctly read as neutral current adjustment rather than Autosens being disabled; non-1 ratios (0.79-0.98) confirm Dynamic ISF is actively adjusting sensitivity. Effective variable_sens swings widely (about 27.8 to 178.7 mg/dL/U) against a flat 56 mg/dL/U base ISF, plausibly explaining inconsistent bolus outcomes noted earlier, but whether this reactivity is appropriate or excessive cannot yet be judged. The carbohydrate absorption model settings (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) are never exercised since COB is always zero in every sampled loop status, so this group remains functionally untested rather than confirmed adequate.

analysis_steps.findings: aaps_profile.analysis_context declares meal_strategies as an empty list with no prebolus_minutes, immediate_bolus_percent, or e-carb fields present anywhere in the package; this is a genuine absence of a declared strategy, not an interpretation gap. Observed telemetry independently shows zero carbohydrate entries and no meal-linked bolus type anywhere in the sampled treatments or therapy_response_windows; every sampled dose is a Correction Bolus or Temp Basal. Declared and observed data are consistent in showing no structured meal-announcement workflow. A recurring shape across many therapy_response_windows shows glucose rising substantially in the first 60-180 minutes after a small correction, consistent with unannounced-meal detection lag through UAM, with several windows later overshooting into hypoglycemia at 120-360 minutes, suggesting IOB stacking compounded by the 10-hour DIA once automation responds to a rise that had no lead time.
data_gaps: No declared prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, or carbohydrate amounts to compare against observed glucose response

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries is 0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; no e-carb entries exist anywhere in the package, so e-carb amount, start offset, and duration cannot be assessed and must not be inferred from any aggregate value. Two dates (2026-08-14, 2026-08-17, 2026-08-20 GLP-1 notes) show more prolonged continuing glucose rises through 240 minutes rather than a typical peak-then-decline shape, consistent with GLP-1's known effect on gastric emptying and treated as a distinct pattern rather than averaged into general meal-response evidence. The 2026-08-19 excursion following a logged pump Occlusion and Pump Error is treated as a device-delivery artifact rather than an absorption-pattern signal.

analysis_steps.findings: Across all stages, the dominant limiting factor is the complete absence of carbohydrate data, which blocks carb ratio verification and meal-timing analysis and confounds interpretation of basal, ISF, and automation behavior. Several notable excursions (2026-08-14 rebound, 2026-08-19 pump error) have plausible non-profile causes and should not drive parameter changes. Dynamic ISF variability, not Autosens or a base ISF defect, is the best-supported explanation for inconsistent correction outcomes. Time below range (5.1%) and repeated hypoglycemia clusters linked to delayed correction effects (10-hour DIA, frequent SMB) represent the most safety-relevant unresolved pattern. Given these dependencies and confounders, no profile or automation parameter change is currently well-supported; the safest and most conservative next step is establishing basic carbohydrate logging before any basal, CR, ISF, DIA, or automation strength adjustment is considered, followed by sequential, one-at-a-time verification of hypotheses raised in earlier stages.

implementation_steps: Review this analysis with a diabetes care provider before making any change; do not modify AAPS settings automatically from this report.
Begin logging approximate carbohydrate amounts and timestamps for representative meals to unblock carb ratio and meal-timing verification.
Once carb-linked data is available, re-review the 12:00-17:00 local hyperglycemia pattern and the overnight and evening hypoglycemia patterns to separate meal, IOB, and basal effects.
If a basal, ISF, CR, DIA, or automation change is later considered supported, change only one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely for several days before making a further change.

Reassess time below range and hypoglycemia clusters after any change to confirm the change moved outcomes in the intended direction before proceeding to the next item.
education: Autosens and Dynamic ISF are distinct sensitivity mechanisms in AAPS; a sensitivity_ratio near 1 indicates a neutral current adjustment rather than Autosens being disabled or absent.

UAM (unannounced meal) detection allows the loop to respond to glucose rises even without logged carbohydrates, but it inherently reacts after a rise has begun rather than preventing it in advance like a pre-meal bolus.

Insulin-on-board and Duration of Insulin Action together determine how long a correction or meal bolus continues to lower glucose; a longer DIA can extend this effect well beyond the original rise, which is relevant to delayed hypoglycemia after corrections.

Time below range and coefficient of variation are both useful complements to time in range and average glucose, since a high time-in-range percentage can still coexist with clinically relevant hypoglycemia or high variability.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; it does not constitute medical advice and does not replace guidance from a qualified healthcare professional.
Every proposed change should be independently verified and discussed with a diabetes care provider before being made.
Change only one setting at a time and monitor glucose closely for several days after each change before making another.
Do not change AAPS settings automatically based on this report; all changes require manual review and action by the user and their care team.

Given the observed hypoglycemia clusters and time below range above a typical 4% threshold, extra caution and closer monitoring are warranted before considering any change that could further affect insulin dosing.
